title: Sequence variations in PCSK9, low LDL, and protection against coronary heart disease
authors: Cohen JC, Boerwinkle E, Mosley TH, Hobbs HH
population: Participants of the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study, aged 45 to 64 years at entry: 3363 Black and 9524 White subjects
funder: Supported by the Donald W. Reynolds Foundation, the W.M. Keck Foundation, and the Le Ducq Foundation; by a grant (HL 20948) from the National Institutes of Health; and as a collaborative study by contracts (N01-HC-55015, N01-HC-55016, N01-HC-55018, N01-HC-55019, N01-HC-55020, N01-HC-55021, and N01-HC-55022) with the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.
authorConflicts: No potential conflict of interest relevant to this article was reported.
result: Of 3363 Black participants, 2.6% carried the PCSK9 nonsense mutation Y142X or C679X (allele frequencies 0.8% and 1.8%), and their mean LDL cholesterol was 28% lower than in non-carriers. Over the 15-year follow-up, coronary heart disease (myocardial infarction, fatal coronary heart disease or coronary revascularisation) occurred in 1 of 85 carriers (1.2%) against 9.7% of non-carriers (P = 0.008); the age- and sex-adjusted hazard ratio was 0.11 (95% CI 0.02 to 0.81; P = 0.03). Of 9524 White participants, 3.2% carried PCSK9 R46L, which was associated with 15% lower LDL cholesterol and coronary events in 6.3% against 11.8% (hazard ratio 0.50, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.79; P = 0.003).
